about: A labelled corpus for the deterministic half of Nexus understanding.
Each case is a room window plus the anchor message a pass would be about,
and the reading the server should reach. The harness in tools/eval_intent.py
scores it; tests/test_intent_eval.py holds the floor.
expect.expression_kind  the deictic kind the resolver should find ('' for none)
expect.referent         the Telegram id the message points at, or null
expect.requires_resolution  whether the text alone leaves the referent open
expect.ambiguous        whether the server should report it could not tell
expect.addressed        whether addressing.addressed should fire
A note on `ambiguous` and an empty room: with no window there is nothing to
be ambiguous *between*, so the flag is false and the render says the server
found no candidate. That is a different reading from 'these two are too
close', and the corpus keeps them distinct on purpose.
expect.when             the time word's direction ('', past, now, future, repeat)
expect.when_unit        its granularity ('' or minute/hour/day/week/month/year)
expect.when is '' for a message with no time word, and a claimed reading
there is a false positive: the server would be placing a time nobody stated.
expect.state            the room-state reading:
.edges                the reply edges [[source_id, target_id]], oldest first
.focus                the target the replies converge on (0 when none)
.relation             '' / continues / shifts / unclear — scored only where
labelled, because it is a reading rather than a record
expect.entities         the things a demonstrative may point at:
.newest_media         the kind of the newest media row ('' when none)
.has_link             whether a URL is in the window
.named                the class the message names ('' / media / link /
message) — scored only where labelled
expect.request          the directive the anchor uses, and its direction:
.directive            the word that makes it an instruction, quoted
.polarity             '' / affirmative / negated — '' when a negation
is present that the reader cannot scope
.manner               '' / command / request
— scored only where labelled, like `state.relation`
Every case carries expect.entities, so a window with no media and no link says
so explicitly rather than leaving the fact to a default — the same rule
expect.when follows. A window row with media or a link but no label would
otherwise read in the report as a false positive in the reader.
expect.object         what the request acts on:
.kind               '' / person / media / link / message / thing —
the class, where 'thing' means a thing whose
kind the message does not state
.source             '' / named / pointed / verb — how the server knows
— scored only where labelled, like `state.relation`

cases.note: A reply to رضا and «اینو» — the id is the answer, not a candidate.
Colloquial object form: the clitic is reported, because it is checked with the explicit person-words before any bare demonstrative.
«این کاربر» as a reply — person kind, and the edge still settles it.
No demonstrative at all: the object is the clitic on the verb.
«بنش کن» with one person having just spoken.
No reply edge, but the instruction names رضا.
The instruction states the Telegram id outright.
«ادمینه» with exactly one administrator in the room.
«ادمینه» with two administrators is not a referent — ask.
A member spoke more recently, but «ادمینه» is the administrator.
«همون کاربر» — three replies in a row aimed at رضا.
«ساکتش کن» — the clitic «ـش» is a pronoun, and the room has been replying to رضا.
«همون کاربر», but the room's replies are split between رضا and سارا — the anaphor does not settle it.
Three people spoke moments ago and nobody was replied to — do not guess.
One person spoke just before; still not a confident referent alone.
«قبلیش» points backwards; the kind is recorded even when weak.
Persian and English in one sentence: «این user».
A Latin role word with a Persian instruction.
Fully English phrasing with a Persian room.
Ordinary conversation points at nobody.
An explicit name needs no resolution — the transcript already carries it.
A price question is not a person reference.
A word ending in «و» must not be read as a demonstrative.
A bare action stem has no object; only the clitic does.
Nexus called by name, with an instruction.
The name written the way a group writes it.
The object marker attached to the name, and a clitic on the verb.
A quotation about Nexus is a mention, not a call: the name is the subject of a reporting verb.

anchor.name: رضا
anchor.text: نکسوس گفت که اینو بن کنه

cases.note: A quotation about Nexus is a mention, not a call: the name is the subject of a reporting verb.

Talking about Nexus mid-sentence: the name is the object of the preposition «با», so the sentence is about the assistant rather than addressed to it. It used to be the corpus's one known gap — the strong grade read it as a call and the assistant would answer a statement that was not for it. A name immediately after a preposition is now a mention; the weak grade is unchanged, so the line still reaches the model as context.

The same reading in the mixed text a group actually writes: «with nexus» is a prepositional phrase, so the message is about the assistant. The English half of the preposition list exists for exactly this, and it is deliberately short — «to» and «for» are absent because both can head a line that addresses somebody.

The case the demotion had to protect, and the reason the old gap was left open: the name is in the middle of the message and this is still a call, because «میشه» is not a preposition. It was pinned only in a unit test; it is in the corpus now so the measurement holds both sides of the rule at once.

The boundary, stated rather than hidden: «از نکسوس بپرس» is a third-person instruction to the room — ask Nexus — so the message is about the assistant and the strong grade demotes it. A group that wants the assistant itself says «نکسوس، ...». The weak grade still marks the line for the model, so the message is not silenced; only the immediate reply is.
A member addressing Nexus is addressed, even though they cannot act.
A misspelled instruction still carries its deictic.
A zero-width non-joiner inside the phrase must not split it.
Arabic yeh/kaf folded to Persian before matching.
A correction that names the person it corrects to.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: نه منظورم مهدی بود، اینو بن کن

cases.note: A sudden unrelated message carries no person reference.
A temporal word is not a person reference.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: قبلاً گفتم که اینکار رو نکنید

cases.note: A chain of replies between two people; the edge names the target.
The owner's instruction with a reply edge is the confident case.
An administrator's instruction behaves the same as the owner's.
Slang for muting, with a reply edge.
A plain question with a question mark.
Colloquial «چخبر؟» — a question with no question word.
A greeting, not an instruction.
Reporting what somebody else said — not an order to Nexus.
A correction with no question and no directive.
An ordinary imperative whose verb is in no lexicon; «کن» carries it.
A Persian/English directive.
A follow-up directive built on «بده».
IMPLICIT INTENT, left as a known gap: a complaint that asks for nothing in words. No deterministic marker fires, and inventing one would fire on every complaint in the room.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: یکی اینجا خیلی داره شلوغ میکنه

cases.note: An ordinary statement. The server abstains rather than guess.
A polite request phrased as a question. Read as a question, because the mark is the marker that decides and second-guessing it needs semantics — recorded as a boundary, not a bug.
«محدوده کیه» — «محدوده» is «محدود» + the copula, not a directive; the question word is «کیه».
«چرا ساکته؟» — «ساکته» is «ساکت» + the copula, an ordinary question, not an order.
«فایل پاکه؟» — «پاکه» is «پاک» + the copula; the thing is deleted, nobody was told to delete.
«باید یه کاری کنه» — «کنه» is the subjunctive, not the imperative «کن»; a wish is not an order.
A question with a reply pointing at it is not open.
A question nothing replies to stays open.
Two questions, one answered: only the unanswered one is reported.
«همین الان» is the present moment, read from the server's clock.
«چند دقیقه پیش» points back at a scale of minutes and states no count.
«امروز» is the present, at a scale of days.

«فردا» points forwards, at a scale of days. The reading was always right; the sentence was not — it read «about 1 day(s) ago», so the block stated a direction and then contradicted it in the same line. The four cases below cover the other magnitude branches of the same defect.
A future span of two days, so the magnitude is not a constant one. The sentence must say «about 2 day(s) from now»: a magnitude worded as an age is the defect this pins.
The week branch of the future span, which is a different magnitude band from the day one.
The month branch, whose unit span is labelled approximate — «at a scale of months (about)» — so the sentence carries two approximations and must not add a third by calling it an age.
The year branch, the largest band. All four are labelled so the harness scores a sentence per magnitude, not one sentence that happens to work for days.
A question whose time word points back a day.
«اون موقع» points back at a time the room established; no scale stated.
«هنوز» is about the present state — "still has not".
«دوباره» says this has happened before; a direction the words state.
No time word at all: the reading is empty, not wrong.
«هفته پیش» points back a week.
A time word in a Persian/English mixed sentence.
A colloquial question whose time word is «دیشب».
«فردا اون موقع» is the future: the word that states a direction decides.
«همین‌الان» with the ZWNJ is the same present moment.
«چند وقت پیش» is "a while ago": a direction and no scale.
«چند ساعت پیش» is a duration, not a question — the noun after «چند» decides.
Two people reply to the same person: that is a convergence, and the anchor continues the file thread.
One reply edge is reported but is not called a convergence.
No reply edges at all, and the anchor still continues the thread.
A substantive message that shares no content word: a change of subject.
A shared noun is the evidence, and it is reported.
Replies split between two people: the focus is the more recent, and the short anchor is not judged.
The anchor's own reply edge is in the graph even with no window, and there is nothing before it to continue.
Two shared content words, both reported.
A two-word message shares nothing with anything and is not judged.
A reply chain, and the anchor continues the thread it belongs to.
A graph is present and the anchor still changes the subject.

Two things posted; the newest is the one a demonstrative prefers. The anchor names no class, so the person resolver is also scored: «اینو» points at the media, and the request acts on it, so the resolver reports no person at all — not even an ambiguous one. An ambiguous pair here would be a person lead for a request about a file, which is the mistake the object reading exists to remove; entity-media-single already reads the same words with no ambiguity, and this is now the same reading for the same reason.
A photo was posted and the anchor points at it.
The message names the class, and the link is in the window.
«فایل» names the media class.
«پیام» names a message, so the reply target is stated.
A demonstrative and nothing to point at: the block renders nothing.
A link with no class named.

A link is not a media row: the newest media is still the photo. As in entity-media-newest, the bare «اینو» points at the thing the request acts on, so the person resolver offers nobody rather than a tied pair — two speakers in the window no longer make a person question out of a request about a thing.
A question mark after a thing noun. Before the tokenizer fix «لینک؟» was one token, so the noun was missed and the person resolver offered the room's members for a message about a link.
«پیام؟» names a message, so the reply target is stated — the same reading «پیام» gives without the mark.
A name at the very end of the message, with the question mark attached. Before the fix «سارا؟» was one token, the name was never matched, and the resolver returned the more recent speaker instead.
A greeting with a question mark is still a greeting. Before the fix «ممنون؟» was one token, so the greeting lexicon missed it and the mark alone made it a question.
A correction with a question mark is still a correction — and correction outranks question, so the precedence only sees it once the token is clean.
The one shared content word carries the question mark. Before the fix «چنده؟» was not «چنده», the two messages shared nothing, and the thread read as a topic shift.
The dangerous pair. «بنش نکن» is built on the same directive as «بنش کن» and asks for the opposite; the act reader alone reads both as an instruction.
«ساکتش نکن» — the object clitic is inside the directive and the prohibitor follows it.
A polite request NOT to act — the case the module exists for. Reading it as a request to ban is the worst mistake available here.
The politeness word comes after the prohibitor, so the prohibition is still the token right after the directive.

The plural prohibitor «نکنید», which is what a room writes to several administrators. The clitic «ـش» points at the file, not at a person, so the message names a thing and leaves no person open — the referent column is not exercised here on purpose.

English puts the negator before the verb, and the tokenizer splits the apostrophe: «don't» arrives as «don» + «t». Without the look-back window this read as a plain instruction to ban. The Persian reader finds no deictic expression in an English sentence, and the label says so rather than claiming a resolution the server does not make.
The other half of the pair: a bare imperative with nothing negating it.
A polite request, with nothing negating it.
The English affirmative, for the pair with polarity-negated-english.
A negation that has nothing to do with the directive. The reader abstains rather than claiming the message asks for the action — the fail-safe direction.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: این آدم خوب نیست، بنش کن

cases.note: «نه بنش کن» is 'no, ban him' — a disagreement, not a negation. In Persian the negator of a directive follows it, so a Persian word before the directive never makes it negated; it only costs an abstention.
The message names the thing it acts on, so the object needs no inference.
The same, for a link: the noun is the strongest evidence and it wins.
And for a message.
The clitic carries the object and the verb says it is a thing, so the object is the media row the room holds. Before this reader the same message handed the model a person.
The same shape with a second content verb, because the reading must come from the verb and not from one lucky word.
A bare demonstrative with a content verb, in a room whose newest thing is a link rather than a media row.
The verb says a thing, and the message points at nothing in particular: the kind is stated as unknown rather than guessed from the room.
The same shape as object-thing-pointed and the opposite side: «ساکت» acts on a member.
A person verb with a bare demonstrative: the object is a person.
The politeness frame does not change the side of the verb.
A generic imperative carries no side, so the reader abstains. Before this reader the same message handed the model a person.
No directive, so no object — the abstention is silent, not a line in the prompt.
The object is read the same way under a negation: the direction and the target are independent readings and both are reported.
A demonstrative bound to a config is a determiner, not a person pronoun.
The same guard for a server noun, with a different verb.
Persian demonstrative, English thing noun — the mixed half of the room.
